meta.title: The Sims Mod Manager: free mod manager for The Sims 1, 2, 3, 4 & Medieval
hero.h1:
All your Sims mods,
finally organized.
hero.sub: A free desktop app that turns your mods folder into a proper library. For The Sims 1, 2, 3, 4 & Medieval, on Windows, macOS and Linux.
hero.eyebrow: Free forever · no account · never deletes your files
themes.h2: The app dresses up for every game.
themes.lead: Switch games and the whole interface follows: colors, logos, the shape of every button, even the classic Sims 1 UI sounds. Try it right here: this page re-themes with it, and every screenshot is the real app.
themes.cap.sims1: The Sims 1 in its own deep blues, with the chunky chiselled buttons the game had. In the app the original UI sounds come along too.
themes.cap.sims2: The Sims 2 in periwinkle, lit up in the plumbob green the game fills every meter with, and rounded off the way the game rounded it.
themes.cap.sims3: The Sims 3 goes glossy: blue glass buttons on pale panels, the way the game's own dialogs looked.
themes.cap.simsmedieval: The Sims Medieval takes parchment and brass by daylight, and carved dark wood after dark. Both are in the game, a screen apart.
themes.cap.sims4: The Sims 4 library in the app's default mint, flat and modern like the game. The whole page just re-themed with it.
themes.cap.dark: It does dark, too: follow your system, or pick a side in Settings.
features.h2: Everything a mod folder wishes it could do.
features.lead: Stop renaming files by hand and guessing which download broke your game.
features.thumbs.p: The app looks inside your .package files and pulls out the actual artwork, plus a breakdown of what's inside: CAS parts, objects, textures, tuning.
features.toggle.p: Flip a toggle to turn any mod off without deleting it. The file is safely renamed so the game just skips it; flip it back any time.
features.conflicts.p: Installed the same mod twice, or kept an old version next to the new one? Both get badged. The app also looks inside your packages and flags the ones that override each other's resources, the real reason CC breaks.
features.conflicts.art: Another enabled mod has the same file name
features.drop.p: Drop files or whole folders onto the window and they land in the right place. .zip, .rar and .7z downloads are unpacked for you, folder structure kept, readmes and screenshots left out. The Sims 3's own .sims3pack format works too.
features.folders.p: Localized folder names ("Los Sims 3"), the Ultimate Collection, OneDrive-moved Documents, multiple installs: it finds them, or you can point it anywhere.
features.setup.p: No mods folder yet? One click creates it with the files the game needs, like the Resource.cfg framework The Sims 3 requires before mods work at all.
features.search.p: Search your whole library, filter by category, switch between grid and list, and watch live totals for enabled, disabled and conflicting mods.
features.caption: Open any mod to see what's inside it, where it lives, and why it got flagged.
exchange.h3: Made a mod? Put it on The Exchange.
exchange.p: The Exchange is the mod shop built into the app. Publish yours in the creator portal and every player can install it with one click, straight from their library.
exchange.shelvesAlt: The Exchange inside the app: a row of game filters and mod cards with their cover art, creator, size and an Install button
exchange.shelvesCap: The shelves are right there in the app. Filter by game, install without leaving it.
exchange.detailAlt: A listing inside the app with its screenshots, version, size, install notes and an Update button
exchange.detailCap: Every listing brings its screenshots and install notes, and turns into an Update button when the creator ships a new version.
saves.h2: Peek inside a save without opening the game.
saves.lead: See every household, every Sim, and the world's stats, read straight from the save file.
saves.householdsAlt: The Saves screen for The Sims 4 listing a save's households, with the selected household's funds, room count and members
saves.householdsCap: Every save's households, backups included. Open one to see its funds, its house, and who's living there.
saves.statsAlt: The Saves screen for The Sims 2 showing world stats: total Sims, households, net worth, size on disk, photos and a life-stage breakdown
saves.statsCap: World stats for the whole save: population, net worth, life stages, even the highest skill in the save.
packs.h2: Every pack you own, on one screen.
packs.lead: Expansions, game packs, stuff packs and kits, each with its own artwork and what it takes up on disk. The Sims 4 and The Sims 3 can switch one off without moving a single file; the other games list what you have.
packs.shotAlt: The Packs screen for The Sims 4 listing expansion packs with their icons, pack code and size, each with an on/off switch, one of them switched off
packs.cap: A pack you switch off stays installed; the game just stops loading it the next time it starts. Handy for a lighter game, or for working out which pack a mod is really fighting with.
download.lead: Free, with no account and no installer tricks. Pick your platform:
download.winSetup.p: Recommended for most people. Windows SmartScreen may warn because the app isn't code-signed yet; choose More info → Run anyway.
download.winPortable.p: No install needed. Extract the zip anywhere and run sims_mod_manager.exe.
download.macos.p: Signed & notarized by Apple. Open the .dmg and drag the app into Applications, then open it like any other app.
download.linux.p: Extract the archive and run sims_mod_manager. Works with Wine/CrossOver game installs too.
download.requirements: You'll need 64-bit Windows 10 or newer, macOS 10.15 Catalina or newer, or a recent 64-bit Linux distro.
download.note: Every version is built automatically for all three platforms, and the app lets you know when an update is out.
download.smartscreen.p: The installer isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen steps in the first time you run it. Click More info → Run anyway.
download.smartscreen.alt: The Windows SmartScreen warning, with arrows pointing at the More info link and the Run anyway button
games.h2: Every mainline Sims game. And Medieval.
games.lead: Each game keeps its mods somewhere different. The app knows where.
games.sims1: Mods live in the install folder's Downloads directory, not in Documents. The app knows the difference.
games.sims2: Handles the standard EA Games Documents folder and the Ultimate Collection's own folder name.
games.sims3: Needs the Resource.cfg mod framework before any mod loads; the app creates it for you.
games.medieval: Mods live in the install folder, not Documents, and need a Resource.cfg; the app sets both up for you.
games.sims4: Uses the standard Mods folder. Just remember to enable CC & script mods in the game's options.
games.note: Every location is just a smart default; you can point any game at any folder in Settings. SimCity support is on the roadmap, and the app was built so any moddable game can be added.
faq.free.a: Yes. The app is free to download and use, and there's no account, no ads, and no "pro" version. If it saves your Saturday, you can buy the developer a coffee, but that's entirely optional.
faq.safe.q: Can it break my mods or saves?
faq.safe.a: Disabling a mod only renames the file (adding a .disabled suffix) so the game skips it; nothing is ever deleted, and re-enabling restores the exact original file. Your saves are never touched.
faq.smartscreen.q: Windows says the app is unrecognized. Is it safe?
faq.smartscreen.a: The app isn't code-signed yet (certificates are expensive for a free project), so SmartScreen shows a warning on first run. Choose More info → Run anyway. Every download is built and published automatically by GitHub's own servers, so nobody can slip anything into it along the way.
faq.localized.q: Does it work with the Ultimate Collection / localized games?
faq.localized.a: Yes. It detects localized user folders ("Los Sims 3", "Die Sims 2"…), the Sims 2 Ultimate Collection, Documents folders moved by OneDrive, and multiple installs of the same game. If all else fails, you can point it at any folder manually.
faq.report.q: Where do I report a bug or ask for a feature?
faq.report.a: Right inside the app: open Settings → Report a bug (or Suggest a feature) and your app version, OS and current game come prefilled. You can also drop a message on Tumblr.

portal.meta.title: The Exchange · The Sims Mod Manager
portal.meta.description: Publish your Sims mods on The Exchange and players install them in one click, straight from The Sims Mod Manager.
portal.brand.sub: Creator Portal · The Sims Mod Manager
portal.ticker1: The Exchange just opened its doors
portal.ticker2: Alpha: the first mods published here get seen by every player in the app
portal.ticker4: Built into the app every Sims modder already runs
portal.pitch.h1: Share your mods with every player, in one click.
portal.pitch.p: The Exchange is the mod storefront built into The Sims Mod Manager. Publish a mod here and anyone using the app can browse it and install it straight into their game: no downloads folder, no unzipping, no wrong-folder mishaps.
portal.step1.p: Upload your mod with screenshots, a description and install notes.
portal.step2.p: Your listing shows up on The Exchange for that game, looking good.
portal.step3.p: The app downloads it and puts every file exactly where it belongs.
portal.auth.signInSub: Welcome back! Good to see you again.
portal.auth.signUpSub: One minute and your mods are on the shelves.
portal.auth.legal: Only publish mods you made or have permission to share.
portal.auth.err.invalidCredential: That email and password don't match.
portal.auth.err.userNotFound: No account with that email. Create one below.
portal.auth.err.emailInUse: That email already has an account. Sign in instead.
portal.auth.err.weakPassword: Pick a longer password (at least 6 characters).
portal.auth.err.invalidEmail: That doesn't look like an email address.
portal.auth.resetNeedsEmail: Type your email above first, then hit "Forgot password?" again.
portal.auth.resetSent: Reset email sent. Check your inbox.
portal.mods.sub: Everything you've put on The Exchange. Drafts are only visible to you.
portal.mods.emptyP:
The Exchange is brand new and the shelves are waiting.
Publish your first mod and be one of the founding creators!
portal.editor.subtitle: Everything a player sees before they hit install.
portal.editor.name: Mod name
portal.editor.nameHint: The clean, human name. Players see this, not the file name.
portal.editor.groupHint: Publishing the same mod in several colours or sizes? Give every one of them the same set name and the app shows them as one card players pick from. Each variation keeps its own page, link and download count, so you can add colours whenever you finish them.
portal.editor.versionHint: Bump it whenever you upload a new file, so players can tell updates apart.
portal.editor.author: Creator name
portal.editor.descriptionPlaceholder: What does your mod do? What packs does it need? Anything it clashes with?
portal.editor.fmt.hint: Select some text and hit a button, or write the tags yourself: [b]bold[/b], [i]italic[/i], [u]underline[/u], [center]centered[/center], [url=https://…]a link[/url]. Addresses you paste turn into links on their own.
portal.editor.notesPlaceholder: Anything players should do besides installing: game settings to flip, saves to back up…
portal.editor.imagesOpt: (up to 10, and the first one is the cover)
portal.editor.imagesBox: Drop images here or click to choose
portal.editor.imagesHint: PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB each
portal.editor.fileBox: Drop your mod here or click to choose
portal.editor.fileHint: One file: a .package (or other mod file), or a .zip with everything in it
portal.editor.fileNote: Got multiple files or folders? Zip them up: the app keeps your folder structure when it installs. Max 500 MB.
portal.editor.publishHint: Off = saved as a draft only you can see. On = live for every player.
portal.editor.legal: Only publish mods you made or have the creator's permission to share. Listings that aren't yours get taken down.
portal.editor.tip1: A cover shot taken in-game, not a flat render.
portal.editor.tip2: Say which packs are required, up front.
portal.editor.tip3: Name known conflicts: players trust it more.
portal.editor.imageTooBig: %s is over 10 MB. Resize it and try again.
portal.editor.imagesFull: Only %s screenshots per mod, so the extra ones were left out.
portal.editor.fileTooBig: That file is over 500 MB. The alpha caps uploads there, so try splitting it up.
portal.editor.needFile: Pick the mod file to upload. That is the part players install!
portal.editor.deleteConfirm: Take this mod off The Exchange and delete its files? Players who installed it keep their copy.
portal.footer: The Exchange is part of The Sims Mod Manager, the free, open mod manager for The Sims 1, 2, 3, 4 & Medieval.
